data.narrative:
Freeform, a Series B robotics and manufacturing company founded by Erik Palitsch, has raised $125M+ to date. The valuation analysis draws on a peer set of three same-stage, same-sector comparables: Generalist AI ($2.0B), Bedrock Robotics ($1.8B), and Dexterity ($1.6B), supplemented by a broader universe of eight private peers and one public comparable (277810.KQ).

Two methods were applied to triangulate value. The stage-progression method, using total raised as a proxy base and applying a 1.9x multiplier typical of Series B progression, yields $238M. The peer-median approach uses the median valuation of the three direct comparables at $1.8B, with a range spanning $1.6B to $2.0B. This method reflects market pricing for later-stage robotics companies with demonstrated traction.

The triangulated analysis supports a valuation range of $202M (floor, derived from stage-progression) to $2.0B (ceiling, peer maximum), with a median estimate of $994M. The substantial spread reflects genuine uncertainty: stage-progression implies Freeform trades at a discount to peers, while peer-median assumes closer alignment with funded cohort valuations. Key uncertainties include Freeform's capital efficiency relative to comparables, customer traction and revenue visibility, and whether the peer set adequately reflects company-specific technology or market position. Further diligence on customer concentration, gross margins, and near-term revenue should narrow the range.
